startup.name: Patientdesk.ai
startup.one_liner: AI front & back office agent for dental practices
startup.description: Patientdesk is an AI bookings system that helps healthcare practices make more money. We do this by handling bookings, payments, and insurance to fill up a provider's calendar with high value appointments.

yc_acceptance.basis: Roughly 1 percent base rate. Conditional on acceptance this is a note: a five person team in a crowded but proven category, with measurable booking revenue as a plus and many same wedge YC companies as a minus, so the estimate stays close to the base rate.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly worry that AI receptionists for dental practices are crowded, with Weave, Peerlogic and many YC companies, and that selling to small practices has high churn. The estimate leans on the cohort base rates in stage_benchmarks.md, where later rounds are rare and slow, and on what happened to comparable YC companies such as onederful and newton.

technical_complexity.rationale: Voice agents with scheduling and insurance verification are buildable, but integrations with practice management systems and accuracy on insurance are hard.

takeover_risk.rationale: Incumbents with distribution can ship similar agents quickly. The timeline is an estimate for a well resourced rival with existing distribution and an incentive to copy the idea.

evidence.claim: Weave agreed to buy TrueLark in May 2025 to add AI virtual reception, showing buyers want the function.
Peerlogic and others market 24 hour AI booking to dentists.

pros.evidence: The pitch ties directly to filled calendars.

brand.rationale: The name is descriptive and uses a dot ai suffix, which is now common and hard to own. It will not drive growth or hurt much.

narrative.headline: A sensible product in a crowded dental AI category that probably gets a seed but struggles to stand out later.
narrative.general_summary: Patientdesk sells an AI booking and insurance agent to dental practices. Demand is proven, because Weave bought a rival in 2025, but several YC companies and larger vendors chase the same buyer. With five people the likeliest path is a seed, then a hard Series A. Healthcare cohort data is thin with only 24 researched companies. The step odds are anchored on the 2022 to 2025 B2B cohorts and the older 2018 to 2021 cohort, which differ a lot, so treat the later rounds as wide ranges.

assumptions: No traction or founder facts were provided.
